title: Autosuggest Runbook Curator for Shortflow Recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight service that analyzes historical incident transcripts, operator actions, and playbook executions to autosuggest concise 'shortflow' runbook steps for first-line responders. Scope: (1) an inference pipeline that scores candidate step templates, (2) a curator UI endpoint for Console to preview/accept suggestions, (3) a dry-run harness to validate idempotency and safety, (4) telemetry & audit trail for accepted/declined suggestions. Deliverables: design doc, initial model + rules engine, API and Console preview, 2-week pilot with oncall team, rollout plan. Acceptance criteria: suggestions appear with >=65% precision on hand-labeled validation set; every suggestion includes an automated safety score and a linked replayable dry-run; telemetry surfaces acceptance rate and mean time-to-first-action (MTTFA) change. Out of scope for MVP: fully automated remediation, RBAC per suggestion (handled in a follow-up), multi-org private dataset training. Trade-offs considered: purely rule-based extraction is high-precision but low-coverage; small supervised model improves recall but needs labeled data and privacy controls. We will use a hybrid approach: pattern extraction + lightweight classifier trained on de-identified transcripts. Safety gating: every suggestion must pass an idempotency check and show reversible operation hints. Compliance: artifacts are stored with KMS encryption and access logged. Rollout: feature flagged in Console (pilot orgs -> canary -> GA).
